title: talent-deep-dive-lifecycle-and-benchmarks-2025
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Summary

This playbook describes the full contributor lifecycle at Redwood: from sourcing and hiring, through onboarding and early-impact milestones, to role progression, internal mobility, and offboarding. It combines role ladder checkpoints, measurable benchmarks, and the timeline for benefits and internal tool access. The goal is to provide a single reference for hiring managers, people-ops partners, and new joiners so expectations and operational steps are transparent and repeatable.

Audience
- Hiring managers
- People-ops and talent partners
- New contributors (ICs and managers)
- Team leads and mentors

High-level lifecycle phases
1) Candidate -> Offer (sourcing, interview SLAs, offer approval)
2) Day 0-30 (orientation, account access, first-10 tasks)
3) Day 30-90 (early-impact, first review checkpoint)
4) 3-12 months (competency growth, role certification)
5) Rotation / Mobility windows (internal transfers)
6) Offboarding / Knowledge transfer

Checklist: pre-boarding (people-ops)
- Offer accepted: trigger provisioning ticket (IT) within 4 business hours.
- Badge and laptop order: placed within 24 hours.
- Pre-boarding doc shared: template: onboarding/hello-email-template.
- Mentor assigned: hiring manager nominates within 48 hours.

Onboarding runbook (Day 0–30) — numbered steps
1. Day 0 morning: Welcome sync (30 mins) with manager — goals for first week and first 30 days.
2. Accounts: create and verify SSO, Slack, Google Workspace, Jira, Confluence, GitHub. Target: all accounts functional by EOD Day 0.
3. Developer setup: dev VM or local environment (internal script)
   - Example: curl -sL https://internal-install.redwood.example/install.sh | bash
4. Training block (Week 1): security basics, infra orientation, product overview.
5. First small PR: assigned by team lead by Day 5.
6. 30-day check-in: manager and people-ops conduct a structured retrospective using the 30-day rubric.

Role ladders and milestone mapping
- Individual Contributor tiers: IC1 (Foundational), IC2 (Independent), IC3 (Senior), IC4 (Staff), IC5 (Principal)
- Manager tiers: M1 (First-time manager), M2 (Manager of managers), M3 (Director-level)
- Benchmarks (sample):
   - IC2: delivers projects end-to-end with minimal design reviews; ownership of a small service; mentors new joiners
   - IC3: influences cross-team design, measurable service-level improvements, 2+ mentees
   - IC4: sets technical direction for multiple teams; owns roadmap outcomes

Progression checkpoints and evidence (what we expect)
- Evidence types: shipped PRs, architecture docs, customer-impact metrics, peer feedback, mentoring log, on-call incident leadership
- Promotion cadence: typical earliest consideration at 9–12 months after hire for ICs demonstrating clear impact; exceptions require lead sponsor and people-ops signoff.

Benefits & perks access timeline
| Day | Benefit / Access | Notes |
|-----|------------------|-------|
| 0   | Basic payroll enrollment | Required forms processed on Day 0–3 |
| 7   | Health benefits eligibility | Enrollment window opens; eligibility depends on contract |
| 30  | Commuter/hybrid stipends | Pro-rated first month |
| 90  | Equity vesting begins | Standard grant terms apply |
| 180 | Parental leave (qualifying) | See family leave policy for full details |

Hiring and interview SLAs (operational targets)
- Phone screen scheduled within 72 hours of referral/ATS flag.
- Onsite / loop scheduled within 10 business days after screen.
- Offer approval (level + comp) turnaround within 3 business days for standard roles.
- Target time-to-offer from req open: 28 days for most IC hires.

Internal tools access matrix (high level)
- Role-based baseline: Everyone: Slack, Google, Confluence, Notion-lite; Engineers: GitHub, CI write access after probation; SRE: PagerDuty on-call after training.
- Escalation: If provisioning fails, open ticket via #it-provision and tag people-ops oncall.

Table: access summary (ascii)
| Resource        | New joiner day | After probation | Owner for approvals |
|-----------------|----------------|-----------------|---------------------|
| GitHub write    | Day 3          | Day 30          | Team Lead           |
| Production creds| N/A (shadow)   | Day 90          | Security / Service Owner |
| PagerDuty       | N/A            | Day 60          | SRE Manager         |

Early-impact rubric (30/60/90 check-ins)
- 30-day: environment, small PR shipped, initial feedback loop established.
- 60-day: ownership of a non-trivial feature or operational task; demonstrates collaboration.
- 90-day: measurable outcome tied to team KPIs; mentor responsibilities starting.

Mobility windows and lateral moves
- Internal transfer earliest eligibility: 6 months in current role (exceptions allowed with manager and people-ops approval).
- Transfer steps:
  1. Candidate discussion with receiving manager.
  2. 1–2 interview loops focused on role differences.
  3. Transfer approval: both managers + people-ops sign.
  4. Official HR transfer effective date and new offer letter.

Offboarding & knowledge transfer checklist
- 30 days before: begin transition plan for ICs taking a full-time new employer role (if known).
- Day 0 (last day): revoke access via automated offboard playbook; export ownership, update docs.
- Post-offboard: exit interview and benefits continuation briefing.

Metrics and quality gates (people-ops KPIs)
- Time-to-provision: median target < 48 hours.
- Time-to-first-PR: median target 7 days.
- 90-day retention: target >= 92%.
- Hiring funnel conversion: offer rate target 55%+ for engaged candidates.

Sample templates and snippets
- Quick welcome email (manager):
  Subject: Welcome to Redwood — first steps
  Hi {{name}}, excited to have you. Please join the 10:00 AM welcome call (calendar invite). Your laptop is expected to arrive by EOD Day 1.

- Provisioning CLI sample for internal tooling (for onboarding engineer use):
  rdxctl provision --user "jane.doe@redwood.com" --role engineer --env dev

Owner and escalation
- People-ops: primary owner for lifecycle policy and benefit coordination.
- IT: owner for all provisioning tickets.
- Security: approves elevated access, onboarding security modules.
- Escalation path: manager -> people-ops partner -> Head of People -> CTO for disputed role-level exceptions.

FAQ (short)
Q: How quickly will I get production access?
A: Production credentials are granted on a case-by-case basis after successful probation and a security review; typical earliest is Day 60–90.

Q: Can I apply for internal transfers before 6 months?
A: Discuss with your manager; exceptions are sometimes approved for business-critical moves but require sponsor and people-ops signoff.
